questions.question: What is a stochastic process?
options: A collection $\{X_t:t\in T\}$ of random variables.
A single deterministic number

questions.explanation: A stochastic process is a collection of random variables $\{X_t:t\in T\}$ defined on a common probability space.
questions.source_support: The definition states that a stochastic process is a collection of random variables $\{X_t:t\in T\}$ on a common probability space.

A finite set of event names is not a collection of random variables indexed by $T$.
A probability density at one point is a single function value, not an indexed family.
